error.write_gated: the play timer is running; unlock parental controls temporarily first

error.autocorrect_off: turn on "Synchronize Clock via Internet" in System Settings first
error.state_unknown: the current play-timer state could not be read, so nothing was written
error.not_confirmed: the PIN was not entered, so nothing was changed
error.session_closed: the system closed the parental-control session; try again
error.bad_pin_format: the system rejected the PIN format
error.relock_failed: the console was unlocked but parental controls could not be turned back on: do it now (PIN › Turn parental controls back on)
error.not_applied: the console did not take the change, so the previous settings were put back
error.not_saved: PlayGuard could not save to the SD card what it must put back later, so nothing was written
error.next_step: If it happens again, send a report: Tools › Send a report online.
error.pt_not_understood: the console's play-timer settings are in a format PlayGuard does not understand, so nothing was changed. Send a report: Tools › Send a report online.

error.pctl_not_ready: the parental-control service is not ready yet: wait a moment, then try again

error.pdm_unavailable: the console's play-data service is not available right now; try again in a moment

Suspend the software when the time is up?

At the limit the console shows "Time's up" and suspends the game. Unsaved progress can be lost.

Only warn when the time is up?

At the limit the console shows "Time's up", but the game is not suspended: it can go on.

play_timer.bedtime_note: Applies to every day. At bedtime the console shows the alarm, and may also suspend the software (see "When the time is up"), until play is allowed again. PlayGuard checks that the console reports the new time, and puts the previous settings back if it does not.
play_timer.bedtime_confirm:
Set the bedtime alarm to {} every day?

Play is allowed again at {}.
play_timer.bedtime_confirm_off: Turn off the bedtime alarm for every day?
play_timer.bedtime_end_confirm: Allow play again at {} on every day with a bedtime alarm?

restrictions.note: These are the same settings as System Settings › Parental Controls.
restrictions.none_body: Nothing will be restricted: software of any age rating can be played, and posting to social media and communicating with others are allowed. The daily play-time limits still apply.

clock.why: The play timer relies on the network clock. When it is inaccurate (a console that never reaches Nintendo's servers), set it here from a public time server.
clock.custom_header: NTP server name or IP address
clock.result_spread: Warning: the servers disagree by {} s.
clock.result_none: No server answered. Check the Internet connection.
clock.need_measure: Measure first (a measurement stays valid for 2 minutes).
clock.expired: The measurement is older than 2 minutes. Measure again.
clock.applied_ok: Network clock set. The system reports it as accurate.
clock.applied_pending: Network clock set and read back. The system does not report it as accurate yet.
clock.applied_refused: Not changed: turn on "Synchronize Clock via Internet" in System Settings › System › Date and Time first.
clock.applied_err: Could not set the network clock
clock.report_err_ask: The report of the clocks before the change could not be saved ({}). Set the network clock anyway?
clock.busy: Please wait for the current request.
clock.autosync_off_note: To set the network clock from it, first turn on "Synchronize Clock via Internet" in System Settings.
clock.auto_how:
PlayGuard can only read this setting: it belongs to System Settings, which only the HOME menu can open.

To change it: HOME menu › System Settings › System › Date and Time › Synchronize Clock via Internet.

When it is on, the console clock follows the network clock. Note: when the clock was moved, the console was seen to start today's play time over.
clock.start_off: The network clock is {} off (checked against {}). The play timer counts on it: see the Network clock tab.
clock.guided_body:
The network clock is inaccurate, and the play timer counts on it.

Measure the time against {} now? (The console must be online.) You will then be asked before the clock is set.
clock.guided_fine: The network clock is accurate: nothing to do.
clock.confirm_apply_resets: Changing the clock starts today's play time over: the whole daily limit is available again.
clock.copy: Set the network clock to the console clock...
clock.offline_hint: Without Internet, the network clock can be set to the console clock instead (Console clock, at the top). Check first that it is right: PlayGuard has nothing else to compare it with.
clock.offline_guided: Without Internet, PlayGuard can set the network clock to the console clock instead: {} now. Do it only if that time is right (check it against a phone or a watch).
clock.confirm_copy: Set the network clock to the console clock, {} ({})?
clock.confirm_copy_check: No time server answered, so the console clock is the only source: do this only if it is right. Check it against a phone or a watch first.
clock.confirm_copy_follows: "Synchronize Clock via Internet" is on, so the console clock follows the network clock and may be just as wrong. If it is: turn the setting off, set the date and time in System Settings › System › Date and Time, then come back here.
clock.confirm_copy_sync_after: "Synchronize Clock via Internet" is off: the console clock stays as it is. Turning it on afterwards will no longer make it jump, both clocks then showing the same time.
clock.copied_sync_on: You can now turn on "Synchronize Clock via Internet" (System Settings › System › Date and Time): the console clock will not jump.
clock.copy_implausible: The console clock reads {}: it does not look set. Set the date and time in System Settings › System › Date and Time first (with "Synchronize Clock via Internet" off), then come back here.

pairing.unlink_body:
Unlink the Nintendo Switch Parental Controls companion app from this console?

Otherwise its next synchronization overwrites the limits set here.
pairing.unlink_err: Could not unlink the companion app
pairing.note: While the console stays linked, the companion app overwrites the settings made here at its next synchronization.
pairing.decode: Before unlinking: help decode two settings
pairing.decode_note: Before unlinking, this console can help decode "alarm only" and per-day bedtime (PIN, 2 min): once unlinked, it no longer can.

security.show_pin_body:
Show the PIN on screen?

Anyone looking at the screen can read it: make sure the child is not watching.
security.unlock_body:
Unlock parental controls temporarily?

Restrictions stay off until you lock them again (or until the console restarts). If PlayGuard is closed from the HOME menu meanwhile, it locks them again the next time it starts.
security.delete_body:
Delete all parental controls?

This wipes the PIN, every restriction and the play-time limit. It cannot be undone, but a backup of the settings (not the PIN) is saved on the SD card first: Tools › Restore a backup.
security.rescue_note: The recovery sysmodule is installed: anyone who can edit the SD card can then unlock the console or delete every parental control at the next start. Remove it when you no longer need it (folder atmosphere/contents/4200000000505247).
security.show_pin_change_body:
Change the PIN now?

Someone else may have seen it.

pin_lock.title: Protect PlayGuard with the PIN

notes.off: Anyone who holds the console can change the settings here. Showing the PIN still asks for it.
notes.changes: Anyone can look; changing something needs the PIN (asked again after 5 minutes). Locking again never asks.
notes.open: A lock screen until the PIN is entered, and again after 5 minutes away from PlayGuard. Locking again never asks.

pin_lock.no_pin: Set a PIN first (Set or change the PIN).
pin_lock.locked_body: Enter the parental-control PIN to open it.

console_lock.title: Block all games
console_lock.note_off: Sets every day's limit to 0, so a PIN is needed to start a game — a light block without turning on age ratings or communication limits. It blocks starting games, not the HOME menu or System Settings. Needs a PIN on the console.
console_lock.note_on: Every day's limit is 0: a PIN is needed to play. Turning this off puts the previous limits back.
console_lock.needs_pin: Set a parental-control PIN first: without one, nothing stops a game from starting.
console_lock.on_body: Block all games? Every day's play-time limit becomes 0, so the PIN is needed to start a game. The current limits are saved and come back when you turn this off.
console_lock.off_body: Unblock games? The previous play-time limits are put back.
console_lock.blocks_change: "Block all games" is on: every day's limit stays at 0. Turn it off in the PIN tab first.

rescue.title: Recovery
rescue.section_actions: What would you like to do?
rescue.note: You reached this screen with the RESCUE file, so no PIN is asked here. Set a new PIN or remove the parental controls, then open PlayGuard.
rescue.note_failed: Recovery did not finish, so nothing can be changed from here without the PIN. Try again with the RESCUE file, or remove the SD card and edit the settings on a computer.
rescue.note_refused: Every parental control would have been deleted, but the request file could not be removed from the SD card, so it would have run again at every start. Remove it from a computer, then try again.
rescue.request_kept: The {} file could not be removed from the SD card: until it is, the console is unlocked again at every start. Remove it from a computer.
rescue.note_deleted: Every parental control was removed, including the PIN. Open PlayGuard — you can set it up again from there whenever you like.
rescue.note_no_pin: No parental-control PIN was set, so there was nothing to unlock. You can set one here, then open PlayGuard.

outcome.unlocked: Parental controls were unlocked, so PlayGuard could open.
outcome.no_pin: There was no PIN to recover: no parental-control PIN is set.
outcome.refused: Nothing was deleted: the RESCUE file could not be removed from the SD card.
outcome.unconfirmed: The console does not show the recovery this report describes.

rescue.note_unconfirmed: Nothing can be changed from here without the PIN, and PlayGuard opens as usual. Locked out? Put the RESCUE file back on the SD card with the recovery sysmodule installed, then restart the console.

tools.export_note: Saved in {}. Attach it to a bug report. It never contains the PIN or the serial number.
tools.backup_note: Saves the restriction level, the custom settings, VR mode and the daily play-time limits in {}. The PIN is not saved.
tools.logs_note: Applies to the diagnostic reports, the crash files, the session logs and the links of the reports sent online in {}, each on its own, at start-up and when a limit changes. The newest one always stays.
tools.serial_note_emummc: This emuMMC uses the console's real serial number: if it goes online, Nintendo's servers see it. To blank it, set blank_prodinfo_emummc=1 in atmosphere/config/exosphere.ini and reboot (Atmosphère warns that blanking is not guaranteed to be safe).
tools.patches_note_files: The recommendation is now to use sys-patch: it patches the system at every boot, instead of files that must match each firmware version.
tools.patches_note_redundant: sys-patch is active: the sigpatch files ({}) are no longer needed.
tools.patches_note_not_at_boot: sys-patch is installed but not started at boot: turn it on in the sysmodules overlay (or create atmosphere/contents/420000000000000B/flags/boot2.flag), then reboot.
tools.patches_note_no_log: sys-patch left no log for this boot, so what it patched cannot be checked: set enable_logging=1 in config/sys-patch/config.ini, then reboot.
tools.patches_note_stale: sys-patch's log was written for firmware {} on {} storage: it did not run at this boot.
tools.patches_note_skipped: sys-patch is turned off for this storage: set {}=1 in config/sys-patch/config.ini, then reboot.
tools.patches_note_unpatched: sys-patch did not patch: {}. Update sys-patch for this firmware.
tools.auto_relock: Turn parental controls back on after a change
tools.extra_auto: Put the usual limit back the next day by itself
tools.clock_check: Check the network clock at start-up
tools.compat_ok_info: This firmware has been checked with PlayGuard: every feature is available.
tools.upload_note: Sends a report to a secret gist in your GitHub account (sign in first if needed) and shows its link with a QR code: give it to whoever helps you, or open a bug report with it.
tools.storage_note_emummc: This is emuMMC: sysMMC has its own parental controls, which PlayGuard cannot see from here. Set them there too, or hide the hekate boot menu.
tools.storage_note_sysmmc: This is sysMMC, and an emuMMC is set up on this SD card: it has its own parental controls, which PlayGuard cannot see from here. Set them there too, or hide the hekate boot menu.

games.title: Installed games
games.note: The games the HOME menu cannot start or draw (an icon that keeps loading, "!", a dotted frame), why, and what to do. A on a game for the details.
games.err_list: The installed games could not be listed
games.truncated: Only the first {} games were checked.
games.many: Several games at once: check the SD card for errors on a computer, and that the console started on the same storage ({} now) as when these games were installed. A game installed from sysMMC does not work from emuMMC, and the other way round.
games.remove_body: Removing deletes the game, its update and its add-ons from the console and the HOME menu. Save data stays.

archived.cause: The console lists the game, but nothing of it is installed any more: it was archived, or its files were deleted outside the console.
archived.fix: Install the game again, or remove its entry to clean up the HOME menu.

storage.cause: The game is on the SD card, which the console cannot read right now.
storage.fix: Turn the console off, take the SD card out and put it back, then check it for errors on a computer. Nothing to remove: the files are still on the card.

no_base.cause: Only an update or an add-on of this game is installed, not the game itself.
no_base.fix: Install the game itself, or remove the entry and what is left of it.

files.cause: Files of the game or of its update are missing where they are installed: an installation that was interrupted, or a damaged SD card.
files.fix: Remove the game, then install it again. If several games are affected, check the SD card first.

corrupt.cause: PlayGuard checked its data ({}): the console found corrupt data. The game cannot be played until it is installed again.
corrupt.fix: Remove the game (first button), then install it again. Save data stays.

firmware.cause: The game or its update needs system version {}; this console runs {}.
firmware.fix: Update Atmosphère first, to a version that supports the new firmware, then the firmware: in the other order the console no longer starts. Or install an older version of the update.
firmware.fix_update: Only its update needs it: remove the update to play the game without it (Actions), or update Atmosphère first, then the firmware.

launch.cause: The console refuses to start it: {}. Usually a newer update of the game is required.
launch.fix: Install the game's latest update. If it is already installed, remove the game and install it again.

no_control.cause: The game is installed, but its name and icon cannot be read: the HOME menu shows an icon that keeps loading.
no_control.fix: Restart the console. If the icon still loads, check the data in System Settings › Data Management, or remove the game and install it again.

needs_verify.cause: The console found corrupt data in this game and asks for it to be checked.
needs_verify.fix: Check the data (first button): PlayGuard remembers what it finds. Intact, the game leaves the list; corrupt, it moves to Reinstall.

key_too_new.cause: The game is encrypted with keys this firmware ({}) does not have (key generation {}).

ticket.cause: The game needs a license (ticket) that is not on the console: it was deleted, or the installation did not include it.
ticket.fix: Install the game again from a complete copy that includes its ticket.

launch_version.cause: The console asks for {} of the game, installed earlier. Installed now: {}. The update was removed or did not install completely.
launch_version.fix: Accept the installed version again (Actions), or install the update again.

action.remove: Remove the game from the console

games.remove_update_body: Only the update is deleted: the game, its add-ons and its save data stay, and the console starts the game without the update.
games.remove_addon_body: Only this add-on is deleted: the game, its update and its save data stay.
games.launch_reset: {}: the installed version is accepted again
games.launch_err: Could not change the launch version
games.verify_bad: {}: corrupt data found. Remove the game and install it again.
games.verify_note: Every file of the game is read: a big game takes a few minutes.

group_note.fix: PlayGuard can repair these: A on a game, then its first button.
group_note.verify: The console suspects their data. Checking it reads every file and says whether to install the game again; PlayGuard remembers the result.
group_note.reinstall: Their files are gone or unusable. Save their list, remove them here (an installer counts them as installed until then), then install them again by searching for their name.
group_note.system: The games are fine: the console's firmware or SD card is the problem. Update the firmware, or start on the storage they were installed on.

games.save_list: Save the list of these games
games.remove_all_body: These {} games are removed from the console, with their updates and add-ons, so they can be installed again. Their list is saved first, in PlayGuard's exports folder. Save data stays.
games.select_many: Several games at once (Y on a game)

dev.pt_block_intro:
Save the play-timer settings as they are now, as a reference?

Then change one setting in the Nintendo Switch Parental Controls app, let the console sync, and come back here: PlayGuard lists the values that changed. This is how the settings PlayGuard does not show yet (bedtime, alarm only or suspend the software) can be decoded.

dev.pt_log_note: Every 30 s while PlayGuard is open, one line of what the play timer reports (time left, time spent, 1459, the settings block) in logs/play_timer/log.csv, and one more right after each change PlayGuard makes, saying which. A clock that moved more than the time that went by is noted too. Leave PlayGuard open over midnight, or until the time is up, to see what the console does then. Sent with the diagnostic report.
dev.clear_cache_body:

The game names and icons, the Activity's last figures and the development build list. PlayGuard reads them again from the console when it needs them: at the next start, the Activity tab takes a moment longer.
dev.clear_logs_body:

The crash files, the session logs (all but this run's), the saved diagnostic reports and the play-timer recording. Kept: the links of the reports sent online (the only way to remove them) and the play-timer block reference.
